newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb gets U.S. patent for corn product.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb gets U.S. patent for corn product.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Crop said Tuesday it was granded a U.S. patent for fertile, transgenic corn that is resistent to the herbicide glyphosate.
Glyphosate is the active ingredient in the herbicide, Roundup, marketed by Monsanto Co.
The transgenic, or genetically alterred, corn would allow farmers to spray their fields with Roundup to kill weeds without harming the crop.

"This product patent is a major addition to our portfolio of intellectual property," Bruce Bickner, chairman, said in a statement. "We expect to introduce glyphosate-resistant corn hybrids in the spring of 1998, which would make DeKalb the first in the industry with this product."

DeKalb said that, since the beginning of 1996, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has granted it nine patents, most of which relate to products with herbicide or insect resistance or to the transformation methods used to develop them.
